title: Show HN: Delete yourself from data brokers without a subscription
content:
The thread discusses the launch of **"remove-your-data,"** an open-source tool created by the developer after paid data-removal services failed to adequately protect their personal information.

**Key points include:**

*   **Motivation:** The creator built the tool to provide a transparent, user-controlled alternative to subscription-based services, offering features like verbose logging, custom removals, and a dashboard.
*   **Privacy Concerns:** Users questioned the irony of having to provide personal information to data brokers to facilitate removal requests, noting that this process might inadvertently expose data to additional parties.
*   **Utility & Execution:** The developer argues that open-source workflows offer better transparency and security because users can self-host and audit the code.
*   **Technical Limitations:** Some participants queried how the tool addresses information already indexed by search engines like Google, highlighting the persistent challenge of removing data that has already propagated across the web.
